scenes.setting: On a ship at sea; a tempestuous noise of thunder and lightning

speeches.stage: Enter a Shipmaster and a Boatswain severally.

speeches.speaker: MASTER
lines: Boatswain!

speeches.speaker: BOATSWAIN
lines: Here, master: what cheer?

speeches.speaker: MASTER
lines: Good! Speak to the mariners: fall to ’t yarely, or we run ourselves
aground: bestir, bestir.

speeches.speaker: BOATSWAIN
lines: Heigh, my hearts! cheerly, cheerly, my hearts! yare, yare! Take in the
topsail. Tend to th’ master’s whistle. Blow till thou burst thy wind,
if room enough.

speeches.stage: Enter Alonso, Sebastian, Antonio, Ferdinand, Gonzalo and others.

speeches.speaker: ALONSO
lines: Good boatswain, have care. Where’s the master?
Play the men.

speeches.speaker: BOATSWAIN
lines: I pray now, keep below.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: Where is the master, boson?

speeches.speaker: BOATSWAIN
lines: Do you not hear him? You mar our labour: keep your cabins: you do
assist the storm.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: Nay, good, be patient.

speeches.speaker: BOATSWAIN
lines: When the sea is. Hence! What cares these roarers for the name of king?
To cabin! silence! Trouble us not.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: Good, yet remember whom thou hast aboard.

speeches.speaker: BOATSWAIN
lines: None that I more love than myself. You are a counsellor: if you can
command these elements to silence, and work the peace of the present,
we will not hand a rope more. Use your authority: if you cannot, give
thanks you have lived so long, and make yourself ready in your cabin
for the mischance of the hour, if it so hap.—Cheerly, good hearts!—Out
of our way, I say.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: I have great comfort from this fellow. Methinks he hath no drowning
mark upon him. His complexion is perfect gallows. Stand fast, good
Fate, to his hanging! Make the rope of his destiny our cable, for our
own doth little advantage! If he be not born to be hang’d, our case is
miserable.

speeches.speaker: BOATSWAIN
lines: Down with the topmast! yare! lower, lower! Bring her to try wi’ th’
maincourse.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: A pox o’ your throat, you bawling, blasphemous, incharitable dog!

speeches.speaker: BOATSWAIN
lines: Work you, then.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: Hang, cur, hang, you whoreson, insolent noisemaker! We are less afraid
to be drowned than thou art.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: I’ll warrant him for drowning, though the ship were no stronger than a
nutshell, and as leaky as an unstanched wench.

speeches.speaker: BOATSWAIN
lines: Lay her a-hold, a-hold! Set her two courses: off to sea again: lay her
off.

speeches.speaker: MARINERS
lines: All lost! to prayers, to prayers! all lost!

speeches.speaker: BOATSWAIN
lines: What, must our mouths be cold?

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: The King and Prince at prayers! Let’s assist them,
For our case is as theirs.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: I am out of patience.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: We are merely cheated of our lives by drunkards.
This wide-chapp’d rascal—would thou might’st lie drowning
The washing of ten tides!

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: He’ll be hang’d yet,
Though every drop of water swear against it,
And gape at wid’st to glut him.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: Let’s all sink wi’ th’ King.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: Let’s take leave of him.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: Now would I give a thousand furlongs of sea for an acre of barren
ground. Long heath, brown furze, anything. The wills above be done! but
I would fain die a dry death.

scenes.setting: The Island. Before the cell of Prospero

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: If by your art, my dearest father, you have
Put the wild waters in this roar, allay them.
The sky, it seems, would pour down stinking pitch,
But that the sea, mounting to th’ welkin’s cheek,
Dashes the fire out. O! I have suffered
With those that I saw suffer! A brave vessel,
Who had, no doubt, some noble creature in her,
Dash’d all to pieces. O, the cry did knock
Against my very heart. Poor souls, they perish’d.
Had I been any god of power, I would
Have sunk the sea within the earth, or ere
It should the good ship so have swallow’d and
The fraughting souls within her.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Be collected:
No more amazement: tell your piteous heart
There’s no harm done.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: O, woe the day!

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: No harm.
I have done nothing but in care of thee,
Of thee, my dear one, thee, my daughter, who
Art ignorant of what thou art, nought knowing
Of whence I am, nor that I am more better
Than Prospero, master of a full poor cell,
And thy no greater father.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: More to know
Did never meddle with my thoughts.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: ’Tis time
I should inform thee farther. Lend thy hand,
And pluck my magic garment from me.—So:

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: You have often
Begun to tell me what I am, but stopp’d,
And left me to a bootless inquisition,
Concluding “Stay; not yet.”

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: The hour’s now come,
The very minute bids thee ope thine ear;
Obey, and be attentive. Canst thou remember
A time before we came unto this cell?
I do not think thou canst, for then thou wast not
Out three years old.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: Certainly, sir, I can.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: By what? By any other house, or person?
Of anything the image, tell me, that
Hath kept with thy remembrance.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: ’Tis far off,
And rather like a dream than an assurance
That my remembrance warrants. Had I not
Four or five women once that tended me?

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Thou hadst, and more, Miranda. But how is it
That this lives in thy mind? What seest thou else
In the dark backward and abysm of time?
If thou rememb’rest aught ere thou cam’st here,
How thou cam’st here, thou mayst.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: But that I do not.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Twelve year since, Miranda, twelve year since,
Thy father was the Duke of Milan, and
A prince of power.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: Sir, are not you my father?

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Thy mother was a piece of virtue, and
She said thou wast my daughter. And thy father
Was Duke of Milan, and his only heir
And princess, no worse issued.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: O, the heavens!
What foul play had we that we came from thence?
Or blessed was’t we did?

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Both, both, my girl.
By foul play, as thou say’st, were we heav’d thence;
But blessedly holp hither.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: O, my heart bleeds
To think o’ th’ teen that I have turn’d you to,
Which is from my remembrance. Please you, farther.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: My brother and thy uncle, call’d Antonio—
I pray thee, mark me, that a brother should
Be so perfidious!—he whom next thyself
Of all the world I lov’d, and to him put
The manage of my state; as at that time
Through all the signories it was the first,
And Prospero the prime duke, being so reputed
In dignity, and for the liberal arts,
Without a parallel: those being all my study,
The government I cast upon my brother,
And to my state grew stranger, being transported
And rapt in secret studies. Thy false uncle—
Dost thou attend me?

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: Sir, most heedfully.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Being once perfected how to grant suits,
How to deny them, who t’ advance, and who
To trash for over-topping, new created
The creatures that were mine, I say, or chang’d ’em,
Or else new form’d ’em: having both the key
Of officer and office, set all hearts i’ th’ state
To what tune pleas’d his ear: that now he was
The ivy which had hid my princely trunk,
And suck’d my verdure out on ’t. Thou attend’st not.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: O, good sir! I do.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: I pray thee, mark me.
I, thus neglecting worldly ends, all dedicated
To closeness and the bettering of my mind
With that which, but by being so retir’d,
O’er-priz’d all popular rate, in my false brother
Awak’d an evil nature; and my trust,
Like a good parent, did beget of him
A falsehood in its contrary as great
As my trust was; which had indeed no limit,
A confidence sans bound. He being thus lorded,
Not only with what my revenue yielded,
But what my power might else exact, like one
Who having into truth, by telling of it,
Made such a sinner of his memory,
To credit his own lie, he did believe
He was indeed the Duke; out o’ the substitution,
And executing th’ outward face of royalty,
With all prerogative. Hence his ambition growing—
Dost thou hear?

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: Your tale, sir, would cure deafness.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: To have no screen between this part he play’d
And him he play’d it for, he needs will be
Absolute Milan. Me, poor man, my library
Was dukedom large enough: of temporal royalties
He thinks me now incapable; confederates,
So dry he was for sway, wi’ th’ King of Naples
To give him annual tribute, do him homage,
Subject his coronet to his crown, and bend
The dukedom, yet unbow’d—alas, poor Milan!—
To most ignoble stooping.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: O the heavens!

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Mark his condition, and the event; then tell me
If this might be a brother.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: I should sin
To think but nobly of my grandmother:
Good wombs have borne bad sons.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Now the condition.
This King of Naples, being an enemy
To me inveterate, hearkens my brother’s suit;
Which was, that he, in lieu o’ th’ premises
Of homage and I know not how much tribute,
Should presently extirpate me and mine
Out of the dukedom, and confer fair Milan,
With all the honours on my brother: whereon,
A treacherous army levied, one midnight
Fated to th’ purpose, did Antonio open
The gates of Milan; and, i’ th’ dead of darkness,
The ministers for th’ purpose hurried thence
Me and thy crying self.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: Alack, for pity!
I, not rememb’ring how I cried out then,
Will cry it o’er again: it is a hint
That wrings mine eyes to ’t.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Hear a little further,
And then I’ll bring thee to the present business
Which now’s upon us; without the which this story
Were most impertinent.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: Wherefore did they not
That hour destroy us?

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Well demanded, wench:
My tale provokes that question. Dear, they durst not,
So dear the love my people bore me, nor set
A mark so bloody on the business; but
With colours fairer painted their foul ends.
In few, they hurried us aboard a bark,
Bore us some leagues to sea, where they prepared
A rotten carcass of a butt, not rigg’d,
Nor tackle, sail, nor mast; the very rats
Instinctively have quit it. There they hoist us,
To cry to th’ sea, that roar’d to us; to sigh
To th’ winds, whose pity, sighing back again,
Did us but loving wrong.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: Alack, what trouble
Was I then to you!

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: O, a cherubin
Thou wast that did preserve me. Thou didst smile,
Infused with a fortitude from heaven,
When I have deck’d the sea with drops full salt,
Under my burden groan’d: which rais’d in me
An undergoing stomach, to bear up
Against what should ensue.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: How came we ashore?

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: By Providence divine.
Some food we had and some fresh water that
A noble Neapolitan, Gonzalo,
Out of his charity, who being then appointed
Master of this design, did give us, with
Rich garments, linens, stuffs, and necessaries,
Which since have steaded much: so, of his gentleness,
Knowing I lov’d my books, he furnish’d me
From mine own library with volumes that
I prize above my dukedom.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: Would I might
But ever see that man!

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Now I arise.
Sit still, and hear the last of our sea-sorrow.
Here in this island we arriv’d; and here
Have I, thy schoolmaster, made thee more profit
Than other princes can, that have more time
For vainer hours, and tutors not so careful.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: Heavens thank you for ’t! And now, I pray you, sir,
For still ’tis beating in my mind, your reason
For raising this sea-storm?

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Know thus far forth.
By accident most strange, bountiful Fortune,
Now my dear lady, hath mine enemies
Brought to this shore; and by my prescience
I find my zenith doth depend upon
A most auspicious star, whose influence
If now I court not but omit, my fortunes
Will ever after droop. Here cease more questions;
Thou art inclin’d to sleep; ’tis a good dulness,
And give it way. I know thou canst not choose.

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: All hail, great master! grave sir, hail! I come
To answer thy best pleasure; be’t to fly,
To swim, to dive into the fire, to ride
On the curl’d clouds, to thy strong bidding task
Ariel and all his quality.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Hast thou, spirit,
Perform’d to point the tempest that I bade thee?

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: To every article.
I boarded the King’s ship; now on the beak,
Now in the waist, the deck, in every cabin,
I flam’d amazement; sometime I’d divide,
And burn in many places; on the topmast,
The yards, and bowsprit, would I flame distinctly,
Then meet and join. Jove’s lightning, the precursors
O’ th’ dreadful thunder-claps, more momentary
And sight-outrunning were not: the fire and cracks
Of sulphurous roaring the most mighty Neptune
Seem to besiege and make his bold waves tremble,
Yea, his dread trident shake.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: My brave spirit!
Who was so firm, so constant, that this coil
Would not infect his reason?

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: Not a soul
But felt a fever of the mad, and play’d
Some tricks of desperation. All but mariners
Plunged in the foaming brine and quit the vessel,
Then all afire with me: the King’s son, Ferdinand,
With hair up-staring—then like reeds, not hair—
Was the first man that leapt; cried “Hell is empty,
And all the devils are here.”

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Why, that’s my spirit!
But was not this nigh shore?

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: Close by, my master.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: But are they, Ariel, safe?

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: Not a hair perish’d;
On their sustaining garments not a blemish,
But fresher than before: and, as thou bad’st me,
In troops I have dispers’d them ’bout the isle.
The King’s son have I landed by himself,
Whom I left cooling of the air with sighs
In an odd angle of the isle, and sitting,
His arms in this sad knot.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Of the King’s ship
The mariners, say how thou hast dispos’d,
And all the rest o’ th’ fleet?

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: Safely in harbour
Is the King’s ship; in the deep nook, where once
Thou call’dst me up at midnight to fetch dew
From the still-vex’d Bermoothes; there she’s hid:
The mariners all under hatches stowed;
Who, with a charm join’d to their suff’red labour,
I have left asleep: and for the rest o’ th’ fleet,
Which I dispers’d, they all have met again,
And are upon the Mediterranean flote
Bound sadly home for Naples,
Supposing that they saw the King’s ship wrack’d,
And his great person perish.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Ariel, thy charge
Exactly is perform’d; but there’s more work.
What is the time o’ th’ day?

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: Past the mid season.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: At least two glasses. The time ’twixt six and now
Must by us both be spent most preciously.

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: Is there more toil? Since thou dost give me pains,
Let me remember thee what thou hast promis’d,
Which is not yet perform’d me.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: How now! moody?
What is’t thou canst demand?

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: My liberty.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Before the time be out? No more!

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: I prithee,
Remember I have done thee worthy service;
Told thee no lies, made no mistakings, serv’d
Without or grudge or grumblings: thou didst promise
To bate me a full year.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Dost thou forget
From what a torment I did free thee?

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: No.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Thou dost, and think’st it much to tread the ooze
Of the salt deep,
To run upon the sharp wind of the north,
To do me business in the veins o’ th’ earth
When it is bak’d with frost.

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: I do not, sir.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Thou liest, malignant thing! Hast thou forgot
The foul witch Sycorax, who with age and envy
Was grown into a hoop? Hast thou forgot her?

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: No, sir.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Thou hast. Where was she born? Speak; tell me.

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: Sir, in Argier.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: O, was she so? I must
Once in a month recount what thou hast been,
Which thou forget’st. This damn’d witch Sycorax,
For mischiefs manifold, and sorceries terrible
To enter human hearing, from Argier,
Thou know’st, was banish’d: for one thing she did
They would not take her life. Is not this true?

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: Ay, sir.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: This blue-ey’d hag was hither brought with child,
And here was left by th’ sailors. Thou, my slave,
As thou report’st thyself, wast then her servant;
And, for thou wast a spirit too delicate
To act her earthy and abhorr’d commands,
Refusing her grand hests, she did confine thee,
By help of her more potent ministers,
And in her most unmitigable rage,
Into a cloven pine; within which rift
Imprison’d, thou didst painfully remain
A dozen years; within which space she died,
And left thee there, where thou didst vent thy groans
As fast as mill-wheels strike. Then was this island—
Save for the son that she did litter here,
A freckl’d whelp, hag-born—not honour’d with
A human shape.

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: Yes, Caliban her son.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Dull thing, I say so; he, that Caliban,
Whom now I keep in service. Thou best know’st
What torment I did find thee in; thy groans
Did make wolves howl, and penetrate the breasts
Of ever-angry bears: it was a torment
To lay upon the damn’d, which Sycorax
Could not again undo; it was mine art,
When I arriv’d and heard thee, that made gape
The pine, and let thee out.

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: I thank thee, master.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: If thou more murmur’st, I will rend an oak
And peg thee in his knotty entrails till
Thou hast howl’d away twelve winters.

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: Pardon, master:
I will be correspondent to command,
And do my spriting gently.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Do so; and after two days
I will discharge thee.

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: That’s my noble master!
What shall I do? Say what? What shall I do?

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Go make thyself like a nymph o’ th’ sea. Be subject
To no sight but thine and mine; invisible
To every eyeball else. Go, take this shape,
And hither come in ’t. Go, hence with diligence!

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: Heaviness in me.
speeches.stage: [_Waking._] The strangeness of your story put

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Shake it off. Come on;
We’ll visit Caliban my slave, who never
Yields us kind answer.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: ’Tis a villain, sir,
I do not love to look on.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: But as ’tis,
We cannot miss him: he does make our fire,
Fetch in our wood; and serves in offices
That profit us. What ho! slave! Caliban!
Thou earth, thou! Speak.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Come forth, I say; there’s other business for thee.
Come, thou tortoise! when?

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: My lord, it shall be done.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Thou poisonous slave, got by the devil himself
Upon thy wicked dam, come forth!

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: As wicked dew as e’er my mother brush’d
With raven’s feather from unwholesome fen
Drop on you both! A south-west blow on ye,
And blister you all o’er!

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: For this, be sure, tonight thou shalt have cramps,
Side-stitches that shall pen thy breath up; urchins
Shall forth at vast of night that they may work
All exercise on thee. Thou shalt be pinch’d
As thick as honeycomb, each pinch more stinging
Than bees that made them.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: I must eat my dinner.
This island’s mine, by Sycorax my mother,
Which thou tak’st from me. When thou cam’st first,
Thou strok’st me and made much of me; wouldst give me
Water with berries in ’t; and teach me how
To name the bigger light, and how the less,
That burn by day and night: and then I lov’d thee,
And show’d thee all the qualities o’ th’ isle,
The fresh springs, brine-pits, barren place, and fertile.
Curs’d be I that did so! All the charms
Of Sycorax, toads, beetles, bats, light on you!
For I am all the subjects that you have,
Which first was mine own King; and here you sty me
In this hard rock, whiles you do keep from me
The rest o’ th’ island.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Thou most lying slave,
Whom stripes may move, not kindness! I have us’d thee,
Filth as thou art, with human care, and lodg’d thee
In mine own cell, till thou didst seek to violate
The honour of my child.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: Oh ho! Oh ho! Would ’t had been done!
Thou didst prevent me; I had peopled else
This isle with Calibans.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Abhorred slave,
Which any print of goodness wilt not take,
Being capable of all ill! I pitied thee,
Took pains to make thee speak, taught thee each hour
One thing or other: when thou didst not, savage,
Know thine own meaning, but wouldst gabble like
A thing most brutish, I endow’d thy purposes
With words that made them known. But thy vile race,
Though thou didst learn, had that in ’t which good natures
Could not abide to be with; therefore wast thou
Deservedly confin’d into this rock,
Who hadst deserv’d more than a prison.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: You taught me language, and my profit on ’t
Is, I know how to curse. The red plague rid you,
For learning me your language!

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Hag-seed, hence!
Fetch us in fuel; and be quick, thou ’rt best,
To answer other business. Shrug’st thou, malice?
If thou neglect’st, or dost unwillingly
What I command, I’ll rack thee with old cramps,
Fill all thy bones with aches, make thee roar,
That beasts shall tremble at thy din.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: No, pray thee.
[_Aside._] I must obey. His art is of such power,
It would control my dam’s god, Setebos,
And make a vassal of him.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: So, slave, hence!

speeches.stage: Re-enter Ariel, playing and singing; Ferdinand following.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
lines: Where should this music be? i’ th’ air or th’ earth?
It sounds no more; and sure it waits upon
Some god o’ th’ island. Sitting on a bank,
Weeping again the King my father’s wrack,
This music crept by me upon the waters,
Allaying both their fury and my passion
With its sweet air: thence I have follow’d it,
Or it hath drawn me rather,—but ’tis gone.
No, it begins again.

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: _Full fathom five thy father lies.
Of his bones are coral made.
Those are pearls that were his eyes.
Nothing of him that doth fade
But doth suffer a sea-change
Into something rich and strange.
Sea-nymphs hourly ring his knell:_
Burden: _Ding-dong.
Hark! now I hear them: ding-dong, bell._

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
lines: The ditty does remember my drown’d father.
This is no mortal business, nor no sound
That the earth owes:—I hear it now above me.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: The fringed curtains of thine eye advance,
And say what thou seest yond.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: What is’t? a spirit?
Lord, how it looks about! Believe me, sir,
It carries a brave form. But ’tis a spirit.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: No, wench; it eats and sleeps and hath such senses
As we have, such. This gallant which thou seest
Was in the wrack; and, but he’s something stain’d
With grief,—that’s beauty’s canker,—thou mightst call him
A goodly person: he hath lost his fellows
And strays about to find ’em.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: I might call him
A thing divine; for nothing natural
I ever saw so noble.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: As my soul prompts it. Spirit, fine spirit! I’ll free thee
Within two days for this.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
lines: Most sure, the goddess
On whom these airs attend! Vouchsafe, my prayer
May know if you remain upon this island;
And that you will some good instruction give
How I may bear me here: my prime request,
Which I do last pronounce, is, O you wonder!
If you be maid or no?

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: No wonder, sir;
But certainly a maid.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
lines: My language! Heavens!
I am the best of them that speak this speech,
Were I but where ’tis spoken.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: How! the best?
What wert thou, if the King of Naples heard thee?

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
lines: A single thing, as I am now, that wonders
To hear thee speak of Naples. He does hear me;
And that he does I weep: myself am Naples,
Who with mine eyes, never since at ebb, beheld
The King my father wrack’d.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: Alack, for mercy!

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
lines: Yes, faith, and all his lords, the Duke of Milan,
And his brave son being twain.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: And his more braver daughter could control thee,
If now ’twere fit to do’t. At the first sight
They have changed eyes. Delicate Ariel,
I’ll set thee free for this. [_To Ferdinand._] A word, good sir.
I fear you have done yourself some wrong: a word.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: Why speaks my father so ungently? This
Is the third man that e’er I saw; the first
That e’er I sigh’d for. Pity move my father
To be inclin’d my way!

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
lines: O! if a virgin,
And your affection not gone forth, I’ll make you
The Queen of Naples.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Soft, sir; one word more.
[_Aside._] They are both in either’s powers. But this swift business
I must uneasy make, lest too light winning
Make the prize light. [_To Ferdinand._] One word more. I charge thee
That thou attend me. Thou dost here usurp
The name thou ow’st not; and hast put thyself
Upon this island as a spy, to win it
From me, the lord on ’t.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
lines: No, as I am a man.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: There’s nothing ill can dwell in such a temple:
If the ill spirit have so fair a house,
Good things will strive to dwell with ’t.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: I’ll manacle thy neck and feet together:
Sea-water shalt thou drink; thy food shall be
The fresh-brook mussels, wither’d roots, and husks
Wherein the acorn cradled. Follow.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
lines: No;
I will resist such entertainment till
Mine enemy has more power.

speeches.stage: [_He draws, and is charmed from moving._]

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: O dear father!
Make not too rash a trial of him, for
He’s gentle, and not fearful.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: What! I say,
My foot my tutor? Put thy sword up, traitor;
Who mak’st a show, but dar’st not strike, thy conscience
Is so possess’d with guilt: come from thy ward,
For I can here disarm thee with this stick
And make thy weapon drop.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: Beseech you, father!

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Hence! Hang not on my garments.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: Sir, have pity;
I’ll be his surety.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Silence! One word more
Shall make me chide thee, if not hate thee. What!
An advocate for an impostor? hush!
Thou think’st there is no more such shapes as he,
Having seen but him and Caliban: foolish wench!
To th’ most of men this is a Caliban,
And they to him are angels.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: My affections
Are then most humble; I have no ambition
To see a goodlier man.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Thy nerves are in their infancy again,
And have no vigour in them.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
lines: So they are:
My spirits, as in a dream, are all bound up.
My father’s loss, the weakness which I feel,
The wrack of all my friends, nor this man’s threats,
To whom I am subdued, are but light to me,
Might I but through my prison once a day
Behold this maid: all corners else o’ th’ earth
Let liberty make use of; space enough
Have I in such a prison.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Thou hast done well, fine Ariel! [_To Ferdinand._] Follow me.
[_To Ariel._] Hark what thou else shalt do me.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: Be of comfort;
My father’s of a better nature, sir,
Than he appears by speech: this is unwonted
Which now came from him.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Thou shalt be as free
As mountain winds; but then exactly do
All points of my command.

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: To th’ syllable.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
speeches.stage: [_To Ferdinand._] Come, follow. Speak not for him.
Enter Alonso, Sebastian, Antonio, Gonzalo, Adrian, Francisco and

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: Beseech you, sir, be merry; you have cause,
So have we all, of joy; for our escape
Is much beyond our loss. Our hint of woe
Is common; every day, some sailor’s wife,
The masters of some merchant and the merchant,
Have just our theme of woe; but for the miracle,
I mean our preservation, few in millions
Can speak like us: then wisely, good sir, weigh
Our sorrow with our comfort.

speeches.speaker: ALONSO
lines: Prithee, peace.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: He receives comfort like cold porridge.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: The visitor will not give him o’er so.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: Look, he’s winding up the watch of his wit; by and by it will strike.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: Sir,—

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: One: tell.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: When every grief is entertain’d that’s offer’d,
Comes to the entertainer—

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: A dollar.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: Dolour comes to him, indeed: you have spoken truer than you purposed.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: You have taken it wiselier than I meant you should.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: Therefore, my lord,—

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: Fie, what a spendthrift is he of his tongue!

speeches.speaker: ALONSO
lines: I prithee, spare.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: Well, I have done: but yet—

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: He will be talking.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: Which, of he or Adrian, for a good wager, first begins to crow?

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: The old cock.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: The cockerel.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: Done. The wager?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: A laughter.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: A match!

speeches.speaker: ADRIAN
lines: Though this island seem to be desert,—

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: Ha, ha, ha!

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: So. You’re paid.

speeches.speaker: ADRIAN
lines: Uninhabitable, and almost inaccessible,—

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: Yet—

speeches.speaker: ADRIAN
lines: Yet—

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: He could not miss ’t.

speeches.speaker: ADRIAN
lines: It must needs be of subtle, tender, and delicate temperance.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: Temperance was a delicate wench.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: Ay, and a subtle; as he most learnedly delivered.

speeches.speaker: ADRIAN
lines: The air breathes upon us here most sweetly.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: As if it had lungs, and rotten ones.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: Or, as ’twere perfum’d by a fen.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: Here is everything advantageous to life.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: True; save means to live.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: Of that there’s none, or little.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: How lush and lusty the grass looks! how green!

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: The ground indeed is tawny.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: With an eye of green in’t.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: He misses not much.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: No; he doth but mistake the truth totally.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: But the rarity of it is,—which is indeed almost beyond credit,—

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: As many vouch’d rarities are.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: That our garments, being, as they were, drenched in the sea, hold
notwithstanding their freshness and glosses, being rather new-dyed than
stained with salt water.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: If but one of his pockets could speak, would it not say he lies?

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: Ay, or very falsely pocket up his report.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: Methinks our garments are now as fresh as when we put them on first in
Afric, at the marriage of the King’s fair daughter Claribel to the King
of Tunis.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: ’Twas a sweet marriage, and we prosper well in our return.

speeches.speaker: ADRIAN
lines: Tunis was never graced before with such a paragon to their Queen.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: Not since widow Dido’s time.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: Widow! a pox o’ that! How came that widow in? Widow Dido!

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: What if he had said, widower Aeneas too?
Good Lord, how you take it!

speeches.speaker: ADRIAN
lines: Widow Dido said you? You make me study of that; she was of Carthage,
not of Tunis.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: This Tunis, sir, was Carthage.

speeches.speaker: ADRIAN
lines: Carthage?

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: I assure you, Carthage.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: His word is more than the miraculous harp.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: He hath rais’d the wall, and houses too.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: What impossible matter will he make easy next?

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: I think he will carry this island home in his pocket, and give it his
son for an apple.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: And, sowing the kernels of it in the sea, bring forth more islands.

speeches.speaker: ALONSO
lines: Ay.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: Why, in good time.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: as when we were at Tunis at the marriage of your daughter, who is now
Queen.
speeches.stage: [_To Alonso._] Sir, we were talking that our garments seem now as fresh

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: And the rarest that e’er came there.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: Bate, I beseech you, widow Dido.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: O! widow Dido; ay, widow Dido.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: Is not, sir, my doublet as fresh as the first day I wore it? I mean, in
a sort.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: That sort was well fish’d for.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: When I wore it at your daughter’s marriage?

speeches.speaker: ALONSO
lines: You cram these words into mine ears against
The stomach of my sense. Would I had never
Married my daughter there! for, coming thence,
My son is lost; and, in my rate, she too,
Who is so far from Italy removed,
I ne’er again shall see her. O thou mine heir
Of Naples and of Milan, what strange fish
Hath made his meal on thee?

speeches.speaker: FRANCISCO
lines: Sir, he may live:
I saw him beat the surges under him,
And ride upon their backs. He trod the water,
Whose enmity he flung aside, and breasted
The surge most swoln that met him. His bold head
’Bove the contentious waves he kept, and oared
Himself with his good arms in lusty stroke
To th’ shore, that o’er his wave-worn basis bowed,
As stooping to relieve him. I not doubt
He came alive to land.

speeches.speaker: ALONSO
lines: No, no, he’s gone.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: Sir, you may thank yourself for this great loss,
That would not bless our Europe with your daughter,
But rather lose her to an African;
Where she, at least, is banish’d from your eye,
Who hath cause to wet the grief on ’t.

speeches.speaker: ALONSO
lines: Prithee, peace.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: You were kneel’d to, and importun’d otherwise
By all of us; and the fair soul herself
Weigh’d between loathness and obedience at
Which end o’ th’ beam should bow. We have lost your son,
I fear, for ever: Milan and Naples have
More widows in them of this business’ making,
Than we bring men to comfort them.
The fault’s your own.

speeches.speaker: ALONSO
lines: So is the dear’st o’ th’ loss.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: My lord Sebastian,
The truth you speak doth lack some gentleness
And time to speak it in. You rub the sore,
When you should bring the plaster.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: Very well.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: And most chirurgeonly.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: It is foul weather in us all, good sir,
When you are cloudy.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: Foul weather?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: Very foul.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: Had I plantation of this isle, my lord,—

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: He’d sow ’t with nettle-seed.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: Or docks, or mallows.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: And were the King on’t, what would I do?

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: ’Scape being drunk for want of wine.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: I’ th’ commonwealth I would by contraries
Execute all things; for no kind of traffic
Would I admit; no name of magistrate;
Letters should not be known; riches, poverty,
And use of service, none; contract, succession,
Bourn, bound of land, tilth, vineyard, none;
No use of metal, corn, or wine, or oil;
No occupation; all men idle, all;
And women too, but innocent and pure;
No sovereignty,—

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: Yet he would be King on’t.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: The latter end of his commonwealth forgets the beginning.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: All things in common nature should produce
Without sweat or endeavour; treason, felony,
Sword, pike, knife, gun, or need of any engine,
Would I not have; but nature should bring forth,
Of it own kind, all foison, all abundance,
To feed my innocent people.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: No marrying ’mong his subjects?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: None, man; all idle; whores and knaves.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: I would with such perfection govern, sir,
T’ excel the Golden Age.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: Save his Majesty!

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: Long live Gonzalo!

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: And,—do you mark me, sir?

speeches.speaker: ALONSO
lines: Prithee, no more: thou dost talk nothing to me.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: I do well believe your highness; and did it to minister occasion to
these gentlemen, who are of such sensible and nimble lungs that they
always use to laugh at nothing.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: ’Twas you we laughed at.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: Who in this kind of merry fooling am nothing to you. So you may
continue, and laugh at nothing still.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: What a blow was there given!

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: An it had not fallen flat-long.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: You are gentlemen of brave mettle. You would lift the moon out of her
sphere, if she would continue in it five weeks without changing.

speeches.stage: Enter Ariel, invisible, playing solemn music.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: We would so, and then go a-bat-fowling.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: Nay, good my lord, be not angry.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: No, I warrant you; I will not adventure my discretion so weakly. Will
you laugh me asleep, for I am very heavy?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: Go sleep, and hear us.

speeches.stage: [_All sleep but Alonso, Sebastian and Antonio._]

speeches.speaker: ALONSO
lines: What, all so soon asleep! I wish mine eyes
Would, with themselves, shut up my thoughts: I find
They are inclin’d to do so.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: Please you, sir,
Do not omit the heavy offer of it:
It seldom visits sorrow; when it doth,
It is a comforter.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: We two, my lord,
Will guard your person while you take your rest,
And watch your safety.

speeches.speaker: ALONSO
lines: Thank you. Wondrous heavy!

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: What a strange drowsiness possesses them!

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: It is the quality o’ th’ climate.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: Why
Doth it not then our eyelids sink? I find not
Myself dispos’d to sleep.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: Nor I. My spirits are nimble.
They fell together all, as by consent;
They dropp’d, as by a thunder-stroke. What might,
Worthy Sebastian? O, what might?—No more.
And yet methinks I see it in thy face,
What thou shouldst be. Th’ occasion speaks thee; and
My strong imagination sees a crown
Dropping upon thy head.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: What, art thou waking?

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: Do you not hear me speak?

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: I do; and surely
It is a sleepy language, and thou speak’st
Out of thy sleep. What is it thou didst say?
This is a strange repose, to be asleep
With eyes wide open; standing, speaking, moving,
And yet so fast asleep.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: Noble Sebastian,
Thou let’st thy fortune sleep—die rather; wink’st
Whiles thou art waking.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: Thou dost snore distinctly:
There’s meaning in thy snores.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: I am more serious than my custom; you
Must be so too, if heed me; which to do
Trebles thee o’er.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: Well, I am standing water.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: I’ll teach you how to flow.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: Do so: to ebb,
Hereditary sloth instructs me.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: O,
If you but knew how you the purpose cherish
Whiles thus you mock it! how, in stripping it,
You more invest it! Ebbing men indeed,
Most often, do so near the bottom run
By their own fear or sloth.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: Prithee, say on:
The setting of thine eye and cheek proclaim
A matter from thee, and a birth, indeed
Which throes thee much to yield.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: Thus, sir:
Although this lord of weak remembrance, this
Who shall be of as little memory
When he is earth’d, hath here almost persuaded,—
For he’s a spirit of persuasion, only
Professes to persuade,—the King his son’s alive,
’Tis as impossible that he’s undrown’d
As he that sleeps here swims.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: I have no hope
That he’s undrown’d.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: O, out of that “no hope”
What great hope have you! No hope that way is
Another way so high a hope, that even
Ambition cannot pierce a wink beyond,
But doubts discovery there. Will you grant with me
That Ferdinand is drown’d?

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: He’s gone.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: Then tell me,
Who’s the next heir of Naples?

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: Claribel.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: She that is Queen of Tunis; she that dwells
Ten leagues beyond man’s life; she that from Naples
Can have no note, unless the sun were post—
The Man i’ th’ Moon’s too slow—till newborn chins
Be rough and razorable; she that from whom
We all were sea-swallow’d, though some cast again,
And by that destiny, to perform an act
Whereof what’s past is prologue, what to come
In yours and my discharge.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: What stuff is this! How say you?
’Tis true, my brother’s daughter’s Queen of Tunis;
So is she heir of Naples; ’twixt which regions
There is some space.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: A space whose ev’ry cubit
Seems to cry out “How shall that Claribel
Measure us back to Naples? Keep in Tunis,
And let Sebastian wake.” Say this were death
That now hath seiz’d them; why, they were no worse
Than now they are. There be that can rule Naples
As well as he that sleeps; lords that can prate
As amply and unnecessarily
As this Gonzalo. I myself could make
A chough of as deep chat. O, that you bore
The mind that I do! What a sleep were this
For your advancement! Do you understand me?

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: Methinks I do.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: And how does your content
Tender your own good fortune?

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: I remember
You did supplant your brother Prospero.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: True.
And look how well my garments sit upon me;
Much feater than before; my brother’s servants
Were then my fellows; now they are my men.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: But, for your conscience.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: Ay, sir; where lies that? If ’twere a kibe,
’Twould put me to my slipper: but I feel not
This deity in my bosom: twenty consciences
That stand ’twixt me and Milan, candied be they
And melt ere they molest! Here lies your brother,
No better than the earth he lies upon,
If he were that which now he’s like, that’s dead;
Whom I, with this obedient steel, three inches of it,
Can lay to bed for ever; whiles you, doing thus,
To the perpetual wink for aye might put
This ancient morsel, this Sir Prudence, who
Should not upbraid our course. For all the rest,
They’ll take suggestion as a cat laps milk.
They’ll tell the clock to any business that
We say befits the hour.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: Thy case, dear friend,
Shall be my precedent: as thou got’st Milan,
I’ll come by Naples. Draw thy sword: one stroke
Shall free thee from the tribute which thou payest,
And I the King shall love thee.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: Draw together,
And when I rear my hand, do you the like,
To fall it on Gonzalo.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: O, but one word.

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: My master through his art foresees the danger
That you, his friend, are in; and sends me forth—
For else his project dies—to keep them living.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: Then let us both be sudden.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: Now, good angels
Preserve the King!

speeches.speaker: ALONSO
lines: Why, how now! Ho, awake! Why are you drawn?
Wherefore this ghastly looking?

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: What’s the matter?

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: Whiles we stood here securing your repose,
Even now, we heard a hollow burst of bellowing
Like bulls, or rather lions; did ’t not wake you?
It struck mine ear most terribly.

speeches.speaker: ALONSO
lines: I heard nothing.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: O! ’twas a din to fright a monster’s ear,
To make an earthquake. Sure, it was the roar
Of a whole herd of lions.

speeches.speaker: ALONSO
lines: Heard you this, Gonzalo?

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: Upon mine honour, sir, I heard a humming,
And that a strange one too, which did awake me.
I shak’d you, sir, and cried; as mine eyes open’d,
I saw their weapons drawn:—there was a noise,
That’s verily. ’Tis best we stand upon our guard,
Or that we quit this place: let’s draw our weapons.

speeches.speaker: ALONSO
lines: Lead off this ground, and let’s make further search
For my poor son.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: Heavens keep him from these beasts!
For he is, sure, i’ th’ island.

speeches.speaker: ALONSO
lines: Lead away.

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: Prospero my lord shall know what I have done:
So, King, go safely on to seek thy son.

speeches.stage: Enter Caliban with a burden of wood. A noise of thunder heard.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: All the infections that the sun sucks up
From bogs, fens, flats, on Prosper fall, and make him
By inch-meal a disease! His spirits hear me,
And yet I needs must curse. But they’ll nor pinch,
Fright me with urchin-shows, pitch me i’ the mire,
Nor lead me, like a firebrand, in the dark
Out of my way, unless he bid ’em; but
For every trifle are they set upon me,
Sometime like apes that mow and chatter at me,
And after bite me; then like hedgehogs which
Lie tumbling in my barefoot way, and mount
Their pricks at my footfall; sometime am I
All wound with adders, who with cloven tongues
Do hiss me into madness.

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: Here’s neither bush nor shrub to bear off any weather at all, and
another storm brewing; I hear it sing i’ th’ wind. Yond same black
cloud, yond huge one, looks like a foul bombard that would shed his
liquor. If it should thunder as it did before, I know not where to hide
my head: yond same cloud cannot choose but fall by pailfuls. What have
we here? a man or a fish? dead or alive? A fish: he smells like a fish;
a very ancient and fish-like smell; a kind of not of the newest
Poor-John. A strange fish! Were I in England now, as once I was, and
had but this fish painted, not a holiday fool there but would give a
piece of silver: there would this monster make a man; any strange beast
there makes a man. When they will not give a doit to relieve a lame
beggar, they will lay out ten to see a dead Indian. Legg’d like a man,
and his fins like arms! Warm, o’ my troth! I do now let loose my
opinion, hold it no longer: this is no fish, but an islander, that hath
lately suffered by thunderbolt. [_Thunder._] Alas, the storm is come
again! My best way is to creep under his gaberdine; there is no other
shelter hereabout: misery acquaints a man with strange bed-fellows. I
will here shroud till the dregs of the storm be past.

speeches.stage: Enter Stephano singing; a bottle in his hand.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: _I shall no more to sea, to sea,
Here shall I die ashore—_

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: Do not torment me: O!

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: What’s the matter? Have we devils here? Do you put tricks upon ’s with
savages and men of Ind? Ha? I have not scap’d drowning, to be afeard
now of your four legs; for it hath been said, As proper a man as ever
went on four legs cannot make him give ground; and it shall be said so
again, while Stephano breathes at’ nostrils.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: The spirit torments me: O!

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: This is some monster of the isle with four legs, who hath got, as I
take it, an ague. Where the devil should he learn our language? I will
give him some relief, if it be but for that. If I can recover him and
keep him tame, and get to Naples with him, he’s a present for any
emperor that ever trod on neat’s-leather.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: Do not torment me, prithee; I’ll bring my wood home faster.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: He’s in his fit now, and does not talk after the wisest. He shall taste
of my bottle: if he have never drunk wine afore, it will go near to
remove his fit. If I can recover him, and keep him tame, I will not
take too much for him. He shall pay for him that hath him, and that
soundly.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: Thou dost me yet but little hurt; thou wilt anon,
I know it by thy trembling: now Prosper works upon thee.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Come on your ways. Open your mouth; here is that which will give
language to you, cat. Open your mouth. This will shake your shaking, I
can tell you, and that soundly. [_gives Caliban a drink_] You cannot
tell who’s your friend: open your chaps again.

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: I should know that voice: it should be—but he is drowned; and these are
devils. O, defend me!

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Four legs and two voices; a most delicate monster! His forward voice
now is to speak well of his friend; his backward voice is to utter foul
speeches and to detract. If all the wine in my bottle will recover him,
I will help his ague. Come. Amen! I will pour some in thy other mouth.

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: Stephano!

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Doth thy other mouth call me? Mercy! mercy!
This is a devil, and no monster: I will leave him; I
have no long spoon.

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: Stephano! If thou beest Stephano, touch me, and speak to me; for I am
Trinculo—be not afeared—thy good friend Trinculo.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: If thou beest Trinculo, come forth. I’ll pull thee by the lesser legs:
if any be Trinculo’s legs, these are they. Thou art very Trinculo
indeed! How cam’st thou to be the siege of this moon-calf? Can he vent
Trinculos?

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: I took him to be kill’d with a thunderstroke. But art thou not drown’d,
Stephano? I hope now thou are not drown’d. Is the storm overblown? I
hid me under the dead moon-calf’s gaberdine for fear of the storm. And
art thou living, Stephano? O Stephano, two Neapolitans scap’d!

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Prithee, do not turn me about. My stomach is not constant.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: That’s a brave god, and bears celestial liquor.
I will kneel to him.
speeches.stage: [_Aside._] These be fine things, an if they be not sprites.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: How didst thou scape? How cam’st thou hither? Swear by  this bottle how
thou cam’st hither—I escaped upon a butt of sack, which the sailors
heaved o’erboard, by this bottle! which I made of the bark of a tree
with mine own hands, since I was cast ashore.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: I’ll swear upon that bottle to be thy true subject, for the liquor is
not earthly.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Here. Swear then how thou escapedst.

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: Swum ashore, man, like a duck: I can swim like a duck, I’ll be sworn.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Here, kiss the book. Though thou canst swim like a duck, thou art made
like a goose.

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: O Stephano, hast any more of this?

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: The whole butt, man: my cellar is in a rock by th’ seaside, where my
wine is hid. How now, moon-calf! How does thine ague?

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: Hast thou not dropped from heaven?

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Out o’ the moon, I do assure thee: I was the Man in the Moon, when time
was.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: I have seen thee in her, and I do adore thee. My mistress showed me
thee, and thy dog, and thy bush.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Come, swear to that. Kiss the book. I will furnish it anon with new
contents. Swear.

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: By this good light, this is a very shallow monster. I afeard of him? A
very weak monster. The Man i’ the Moon! A most poor credulous monster!
Well drawn, monster, in good sooth!

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: I’ll show thee every fertile inch o’ the island; and I will kiss thy
foot. I prithee, be my god.

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: By this light, a most perfidious and drunken monster. When ’s god’s
asleep, he’ll rob his bottle.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: I’ll kiss thy foot. I’ll swear myself thy subject.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Come on, then; down, and swear.

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: I shall laugh myself to death at this puppy-headed monster. A most
scurvy monster! I could find in my heart to beat him,—

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Come, kiss.

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: But that the poor monster’s in drink. An abominable monster!

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: I’ll show thee the best springs; I’ll pluck thee berries;
I’ll fish for thee, and get thee wood enough.
A plague upon the tyrant that I serve!
I’ll bear him no more sticks, but follow thee,
Thou wondrous man.

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: A most ridiculous monster, to make a wonder of a poor drunkard!

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: I prithee, let me bring thee where crabs grow;
And I with my long nails will dig thee pig-nuts;
Show thee a jay’s nest, and instruct thee how
To snare the nimble marmoset; I’ll bring thee
To clustering filberts, and sometimes I’ll get thee
Young scamels from the rock. Wilt thou go with me?

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: I prithee now, lead the way without any more talking. Trinculo, the
King and all our company else being drowned, we will inherit here.
Here, bear my bottle. Fellow Trinculo, we’ll fill him by and by again.

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: A howling monster, a drunken monster.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: _No more dams I’ll make for fish;
Nor fetch in firing
At requiring,
Nor scrape trenchering, nor wash dish;
’Ban ’Ban, Cacaliban,
Has a new master—Get a new man._
Freedom, high-day! high-day, freedom! freedom,
high-day, freedom!

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: O brave monster! lead the way.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
lines: There be some sports are painful, and their labour
Delight in them sets off: some kinds of baseness
Are nobly undergone; and most poor matters
Point to rich ends. This my mean task
Would be as heavy to me as odious, but
The mistress which I serve quickens what’s dead,
And makes my labours pleasures: O, she is
Ten times more gentle than her father’s crabbed,
And he’s compos’d of harshness. I must remove
Some thousands of these logs, and pile them up,
Upon a sore injunction: my sweet mistress
Weeps when she sees me work, and says such baseness
Had never like executor. I forget:
But these sweet thoughts do even refresh my labours,
Most busy, least when I do it.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: Alas now, pray you,
Work not so hard: I would the lightning had
Burnt up those logs that you are enjoin’d to pile!
Pray, set it down and rest you. When this burns,
’Twill weep for having wearied you. My father
Is hard at study; pray, now, rest yourself:
He’s safe for these three hours.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
lines: O most dear mistress,
The sun will set, before I shall discharge
What I must strive to do.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: If you’ll sit down,
I’ll bear your logs the while. Pray give me that;
I’ll carry it to the pile.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
lines: No, precious creature;
I had rather crack my sinews, break my back,
Than you should such dishonour undergo,
While I sit lazy by.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: It would become me
As well as it does you: and I should do it
With much more ease; for my good will is to it,
And yours it is against.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: This visitation shows it.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: You look wearily.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
lines: No, noble mistress; ’tis fresh morning with me
When you are by at night. I do beseech you—
Chiefly that I might set it in my prayers—
What is your name?

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: Miranda—O my father!
I have broke your hest to say so.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
lines: Admir’d Miranda!
Indeed, the top of admiration; worth
What’s dearest to the world! Full many a lady
I have ey’d with best regard, and many a time
Th’ harmony of their tongues hath into bondage
Brought my too diligent ear: for several virtues
Have I lik’d several women; never any
With so full soul but some defect in her
Did quarrel with the noblest grace she ow’d,
And put it to the foil: but you, O you,
So perfect and so peerless, are created
Of every creature’s best.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: I do not know
One of my sex; no woman’s face remember,
Save, from my glass, mine own; nor have I seen
More that I may call men than you, good friend,
And my dear father: how features are abroad,
I am skilless of; but, by my modesty,
The jewel in my dower, I would not wish
Any companion in the world but you;
Nor can imagination form a shape,
Besides yourself, to like of. But I prattle
Something too wildly, and my father’s precepts
I therein do forget.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
lines: I am, in my condition,
A prince, Miranda; I do think, a King;
I would not so!—and would no more endure
This wooden slavery than to suffer
The flesh-fly blow my mouth. Hear my soul speak:
The very instant that I saw you, did
My heart fly to your service; there resides,
To make me slave to it; and for your sake
Am I this patient log-man.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: Do you love me?

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
lines: O heaven, O earth, bear witness to this sound,
And crown what I profess with kind event,
If I speak true; if hollowly, invert
What best is boded me to mischief! I,
Beyond all limit of what else i’ the world,
Do love, prize, honour you.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: I am a fool
To weep at what I am glad of.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Of two most rare affections! Heavens rain grace
On that which breeds between ’em!

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
lines: Wherefore weep you?

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: At mine unworthiness, that dare not offer
What I desire to give; and much less take
What I shall die to want. But this is trifling;
And all the more it seeks to hide itself,
The bigger bulk it shows. Hence, bashful cunning!
And prompt me, plain and holy innocence!
I am your wife if you will marry me;
If not, I’ll die your maid: to be your fellow
You may deny me; but I’ll be your servant,
Whether you will or no.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
lines: My mistress, dearest;
And I thus humble ever.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: My husband, then?

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
lines: Ay, with a heart as willing
As bondage e’er of freedom: here’s my hand.

speeches.speaker: MIRANDA
lines: And mine, with my heart in ’t: and now farewell
Till half an hour hence.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
lines: A thousand thousand!

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: So glad of this as they, I cannot be,
Who are surpris’d withal; but my rejoicing
At nothing can be more. I’ll to my book;
For yet, ere supper time, must I perform
Much business appertaining.

speeches.stage: Enter Caliban with a bottle, Stephano and Trinculo.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Tell not me:—when the butt is out we will drink water; not a drop
before: therefore bear up, and board ’em. Servant-monster, drink to me.

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: Servant-monster! The folly of this island! They say there’s but five
upon this isle; we are three of them; if th’ other two be brained like
us, the state totters.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Drink, servant-monster, when I bid thee: thy eyes are almost set in thy
head.

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: Where should they be set else? He were a brave monster indeed, if they
were set in his tail.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: My man-monster hath drown’d his tongue in sack: for my part, the sea
cannot drown me; I swam, ere I could recover the shore, five-and-thirty
leagues, off and on, by this light. Thou shalt be my lieutenant,
monster, or my standard.

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: Your lieutenant, if you list; he’s no standard.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: We’ll not run, Monsieur monster.

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: Nor go neither. But you’ll lie like dogs, and yet say nothing neither.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Moon-calf, speak once in thy life, if thou beest a good moon-calf.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: How does thy honour? Let me lick thy shoe. I’ll not serve him, he is
not valiant.

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: Thou liest, most ignorant monster: I am in case to justle a constable.
Why, thou deboshed fish thou, was there ever man a coward that hath
drunk so much sack as I today? Wilt thou tell a monstrous lie, being
but half a fish and half a monster?

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: Lo, how he mocks me! wilt thou let him, my lord?

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: “Lord” quoth he! That a monster should be such a natural!

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: Lo, lo again! bite him to death, I prithee.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Trinculo, keep a good tongue in your head: if you prove a mutineer, the
next tree! The poor monster’s my subject, and he shall not suffer
indignity.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: I thank my noble lord. Wilt thou be pleas’d to hearken once again to
the suit I made to thee?

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Marry. will I. Kneel and repeat it. I will stand, and so shall
Trinculo.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: As I told thee before, I am subject to a tyrant, a sorcerer, that by
his cunning hath cheated me of the island.

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: Thou liest.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: Thou liest, thou jesting monkey, thou;
I would my valiant master would destroy thee;
I do not lie.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Trinculo, if you trouble him any more in his tale, by this hand, I will
supplant some of your teeth.

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: Why, I said nothing.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Mum, then, and no more. Proceed.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: I say, by sorcery he got this isle;
From me he got it. If thy greatness will,
Revenge it on him,—for I know thou dar’st;
But this thing dare not,—

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: That’s most certain.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: Thou shalt be lord of it and I’ll serve thee.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: How now shall this be compassed? Canst thou bring me to the party?

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: Yea, yea, my lord: I’ll yield him thee asleep,
Where thou mayst knock a nail into his head.

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: Thou liest. Thou canst not.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: What a pied ninny’s this! Thou scurvy patch!
I do beseech thy greatness, give him blows,
And take his bottle from him: when that’s gone
He shall drink nought but brine; for I’ll not show him
Where the quick freshes are.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Trinculo, run into no further danger: interrupt the monster one word
further, and by this hand, I’ll turn my mercy out o’ doors, and make a
stock-fish of thee.

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: Why, what did I? I did nothing. I’ll go farther off.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Didst thou not say he lied?

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: Thou liest.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Do I so? Take thou that.

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: I did not give the lie. Out o’ your wits and hearing too? A pox o’ your
bottle! this can sack and drinking do. A murrain on your monster, and
the devil take your fingers!

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: Ha, ha, ha!

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Now, forward with your tale.—Prithee stand further off.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: Beat him enough: after a little time,
I’ll beat him too.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Stand farther.—Come, proceed.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: Why, as I told thee, ’tis a custom with him
I’ th’ afternoon to sleep: there thou mayst brain him,
Having first seiz’d his books; or with a log
Batter his skull, or paunch him with a stake,
Or cut his wezand with thy knife. Remember
First to possess his books; for without them
He’s but a sot, as I am, nor hath not
One spirit to command: they all do hate him
As rootedly as I. Burn but his books.
He has brave utensils,—for so he calls them,—
Which, when he has a house, he’ll deck withal.
And that most deeply to consider is
The beauty of his daughter; he himself
Calls her a nonpareil: I never saw a woman
But only Sycorax my dam and she;
But she as far surpasseth Sycorax
As great’st does least.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Is it so brave a lass?

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: Ay, lord, she will become thy bed, I warrant,
And bring thee forth brave brood.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Monster, I will kill this man. His daughter and I will be king and
queen,—save our graces!—and Trinculo and thyself shall be viceroys.
Dost thou like the plot, Trinculo?

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: Excellent.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Give me thy hand: I am sorry I beat thee; but while thou liv’st, keep a
good tongue in thy head.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: Within this half hour will he be asleep.
Wilt thou destroy him then?

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Ay, on mine honour.

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: This will I tell my master.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: Thou mak’st me merry. I am full of pleasure.
Let us be jocund: will you troll the catch
You taught me but while-ere?

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: At thy request, monster, I will do reason, any reason. Come on,
Trinculo, let us sing.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: That’s not the tune.

speeches.stage: [_Ariel plays the tune on a tabor and pipe._]

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: What is this same?

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: This is the tune of our catch, played by the picture of Nobody.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: If thou beest a man, show thyself in thy likeness: if thou beest a
devil, take ’t as thou list.

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: O, forgive me my sins!

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: He that dies pays all debts: I defy thee. Mercy upon us!

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: Art thou afeard?

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: No, monster, not I.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: Be not afeard. The isle is full of noises,
Sounds, and sweet airs, that give delight, and hurt not.
Sometimes a thousand twangling instruments
Will hum about mine ears; and sometimes voices,
That, if I then had wak’d after long sleep,
Will make me sleep again: and then, in dreaming,
The clouds methought would open and show riches
Ready to drop upon me; that, when I wak’d,
I cried to dream again.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: This will prove a brave kingdom to me, where I shall have my music for
nothing.

speeches.speaker: CALIBAN
lines: When Prospero is destroyed.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: That shall be by and by: I remember the story.

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: The sound is going away. Let’s follow it, and after do our work.

speeches.speaker: STEPHANO
lines: Lead, monster: we’ll follow. I would I could see this taborer! he lays
it on. Wilt come?

speeches.speaker: TRINCULO
lines: I’ll follow, Stephano.

speeches.stage: Enter Alonso, Sebastian, Antonio, Gonzalo, Adrian, Francisco, &c.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: By ’r lakin, I can go no further, sir;
My old bones ache: here’s a maze trod, indeed,
Through forth-rights and meanders! By your patience,
I needs must rest me.

speeches.speaker: ALONSO
lines: Old lord, I cannot blame thee,
Who am myself attach’d with weariness
To th’ dulling of my spirits: sit down, and rest.
Even here I will put off my hope, and keep it
No longer for my flatterer: he is drown’d
Whom thus we stray to find; and the sea mocks
Our frustrate search on land. Well, let him go.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: so out of hope.
Do not, for one repulse, forgo the purpose
That you resolv’d to effect.
speeches.stage: [_Aside to Sebastian._] I am right glad that he’s

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: Will we take throughly.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: For, now they are oppress’d with travel, they
Will not, nor cannot, use such vigilance
As when they are fresh.
speeches.stage: [_Aside to Sebastian._] Let it be tonight;

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
speeches.stage: [_Aside to Antonio._] I say, tonight: no more.

speeches.speaker: ALONSO
lines: What harmony is this? My good friends, hark!

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: Marvellous sweet music!

speeches.speaker: ALONSO
lines: Give us kind keepers, heavens! What were these?

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: A living drollery. Now I will believe
That there are unicorns; that in Arabia
There is one tree, the phoenix’ throne; one phoenix
At this hour reigning there.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: I’ll believe both;
And what does else want credit, come to me,
And I’ll be sworn ’tis true: travellers ne’er did lie,
Though fools at home condemn them.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: If in Naples
I should report this now, would they believe me?
If I should say, I saw such islanders,—
For, certes, these are people of the island,—
Who, though, they are of monstrous shape, yet, note,
Their manners are more gentle, kind, than of
Our human generation you shall find
Many, nay, almost any.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Thou hast said well; for some of you there present
Are worse than devils.

speeches.speaker: ALONSO
lines: I cannot too much muse
Such shapes, such gesture, and such sound, expressing—
Although they want the use of tongue—a kind
Of excellent dumb discourse.

speeches.speaker: FRANCISCO
lines: They vanish’d strangely.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: No matter, since
They have left their viands behind; for we have stomachs.—
Will’t please you taste of what is here?

speeches.speaker: ALONSO
lines: Not I.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: Faith, sir, you need not fear. When we were boys,
Who would believe that there were mountaineers
Dewlapp’d like bulls, whose throats had hanging at ’em
Wallets of flesh? Or that there were such men
Whose heads stood in their breasts? which now we find
Each putter-out of five for one will bring us
Good warrant of.

speeches.speaker: ALONSO
lines: I will stand to, and feed,
Although my last, no matter, since I feel
The best is past. Brother, my lord the duke,
Stand to, and do as we.

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: You are three men of sin, whom Destiny,
That hath to instrument this lower world
And what is in’t,—the never-surfeited sea
Hath caused to belch up you; and on this island
Where man doth not inhabit; you ’mongst men
Being most unfit to live. I have made you mad;
And even with such-like valour men hang and drown
Their proper selves.

speeches.stage: [_He vanishes in thunder: then, to soft music, enter the Shapes again,

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Perform’d, my Ariel; a grace it had, devouring.
Of my instruction hast thou nothing bated
In what thou hadst to say: so, with good life
And observation strange, my meaner ministers
Their several kinds have done. My high charms work,
And these mine enemies are all knit up
In their distractions; they now are in my power;
And in these fits I leave them, while I visit
Young Ferdinand,—whom they suppose is drown’d,—
And his and mine lov’d darling.
speeches.stage: [_Aside._] Bravely the figure of this Harpy hast thou

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: I’ the name of something holy, sir, why stand you
In this strange stare?

speeches.speaker: ALONSO
lines: O, it is monstrous! monstrous!
Methought the billows spoke, and told me of it;
The winds did sing it to me; and the thunder,
That deep and dreadful organ-pipe, pronounc’d
The name of Prosper: it did bass my trespass.
Therefore my son i’ th’ ooze is bedded; and
I’ll seek him deeper than e’er plummet sounded,
And with him there lie mudded.

speeches.speaker: SEBASTIAN
lines: But one fiend at a time,
I’ll fight their legions o’er.

speeches.speaker: ANTONIO
lines: I’ll be thy second.

speeches.speaker: GONZALO
lines: All three of them are desperate: their great guilt,
Like poison given to work a great time after,
Now ’gins to bite the spirits. I do beseech you
That are of suppler joints, follow them swiftly
And hinder them from what this ecstasy
May now provoke them to.

speeches.speaker: ADRIAN
lines: Follow, I pray you.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: If I have too austerely punish’d you,
Your compensation makes amends: for I
Have given you here a third of mine own life,
Or that for which I live; who once again
I tender to thy hand: all thy vexations
Were but my trials of thy love, and thou
Hast strangely stood the test: here, afore Heaven,
I ratify this my rich gift. O Ferdinand,
Do not smile at me that I boast her off,
For thou shalt find she will outstrip all praise,
And make it halt behind her.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
lines: I do believe it
Against an oracle.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Then, as my gift and thine own acquisition
Worthily purchas’d, take my daughter: but
If thou dost break her virgin knot before
All sanctimonious ceremonies may
With full and holy rite be minister’d,
No sweet aspersion shall the heavens let fall
To make this contract grow; but barren hate,
Sour-ey’d disdain, and discord shall bestrew
The union of your bed with weeds so loathly
That you shall hate it both: therefore take heed,
As Hymen’s lamps shall light you.

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
lines: As I hope
For quiet days, fair issue, and long life,
With such love as ’tis now, the murkiest den,
The most opportune place, the strong’st suggestion
Our worser genius can, shall never melt
Mine honour into lust, to take away
The edge of that day’s celebration,
When I shall think, or Phoebus’ steeds are founder’d,
Or Night kept chain’d below.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Fairly spoke:
Sit, then, and talk with her, she is thine own.
What, Ariel! my industrious servant, Ariel!

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: What would my potent master? here I am.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Thou and thy meaner fellows your last service
Did worthily perform; and I must use you
In such another trick. Go bring the rabble,
O’er whom I give thee power, here to this place.
Incite them to quick motion; for I must
Bestow upon the eyes of this young couple
Some vanity of mine art: it is my promise,
And they expect it from me.

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: Presently?

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Ay, with a twink.

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: Before you can say “Come” and “Go,”
And breathe twice, and cry “so, so,”
Each one, tripping on his toe,
Will be here with mop and mow.
Do you love me, master? no?

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Dearly, my delicate Ariel. Do not approach
Till thou dost hear me call.

speeches.speaker: ARIEL
lines: Well, I conceive.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Look thou be true; do not give dalliance
Too much the rein: the strongest oaths are straw
To th’ fire i’ the blood: be more abstemious,
Or else good night your vow!

speeches.speaker: FERDINAND
lines: I warrant you, sir;
The white cold virgin snow upon my heart
Abates the ardour of my liver.

speeches.speaker: PROSPERO
lines: Well.
Now come, my Ariel! bring a corollary,
Rather than want a spirit: appear, and pertly.
No tongue! all eyes! be silent.

speeches.speaker: IRIS
lines: Ceres, most bounteous lady, thy rich leas
Of wheat, rye, barley, vetches, oats, and peas;
Thy turfy mountains, where live nibbling sheep,
And flat meads thatch’d with stover, them to keep;
Thy banks with pioned and twilled brims,
Which spongy April at thy hest betrims,
To make cold nymphs chaste crowns; and thy broom groves,
Whose shadow the dismissed bachelor loves,
Being lass-lorn; thy pole-clipt vineyard;
And thy sea-marge, sterile and rocky-hard,
Where thou thyself dost air: the Queen o’ th’ sky,
Whose wat’ry arch and messenger am I,
Bids thee leave these; and with her sovereign grace,
Here on this grass-plot, in this very place,
To come and sport; her peacocks fly amain:
Approach, rich Ceres, her to entertain.

speeches.speaker: CERES
lines: Hail, many-colour’d messenger, that ne’er
Dost disobey the wife of Jupiter;
Who with thy saffron wings upon my flowers
Diffusest honey drops, refreshing showers;
And with each end of thy blue bow dost crown
My bosky acres and my unshrubb’d down,
Rich scarf to my proud earth; why hath thy queen
Summon’d me hither to this short-grass’d green?

speeches.speaker: IRIS
lines: A contract of true love to celebrate,
And some donation freely to estate
On the blest lovers.

speeches.speaker: CERES
lines: Tell me, heavenly bow,
If Venus or her son, as thou dost know,
Do now attend the queen? Since they did plot
The means that dusky Dis my daughter got,
Her and her blind boy’s scandal’d company
I have forsworn.

speeches.speaker: IRIS
lines: Of her society
Be not afraid. I met her deity
Cutting the clouds towards Paphos, and her son
Dove-drawn with her. Here thought they to have done
Some wanton charm upon this man and maid,
Whose vows are, that no bed-right shall be paid
Till Hymen’s torch be lighted; but in vain.
Mars’s hot minion is return’d again;
